vBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
vBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2255: Agent mailboxes: issue-addressed delivery contract with drain-on-spawn self-healing (sibling to PAN-2079)

plan.title: Agent mailboxes: issue-addressed delivery contract with drain-on-spawn self-healing (sibling to PAN-2079)
plan.author: agent:gpt-5.5

narratives.Problem: Review/test feedback is persisted to `.pan/feedback/`, but delivery is still addressed to ephemeral agent ids. If the dashboard restarts, the tmux session dies, or a swarm slot id changes between feedback write and push delivery, the system can mark `feedback_delivery_needs_you` and require an operator to hand-deliver a file path even though the durable feedback file exists.
narratives.Proposal: Introduce an issue+role mailbox contract over the existing `.pan/feedback/*.md` files. Feedback producers write mailbox metadata with state `pending`; live push delivery may mark an item delivered, but work-agent spawn/resume always drains pending and already-delivered action-required items into the first prompt and updates the state idempotently. Deacon auto-resume naturally self-heals missed messages because it uses the same resume path. Only after a one-patrol policy window with no eligible work agent does the system escalate to the operator fallback. Close-out summarizes still-pending items in a stale-warning tracker comment before workspace teardown removes `.pan/feedback/`.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No mailbox archive beyond the close-out tracker comment.
- No new durable mailbox store outside existing `.pan/feedback/*.md` files.
- No frontend/operator inbox UI work; PAN-2079 owns the operator surface.
- No browser UAT requirement; verification is backend unit/integration coverage.
- No changes to unrelated conversation message delivery or manual `pan tell` semantics.

autoDecisions.summary: Use embedded metadata in feedback markdown files for mailbox state.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue explicitly says the existing numbered `.pan/feedback/` files are the store and rejects a new archive; embedded metadata keeps the state co-located with the message while preserving human-readable files.

autoDecisions.summary: Default the escalation policy to one Deacon patrol cycle and keep the current stuck marker as the fallback plumbing until PAN-2079's operator inbox API is present.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue names one patrol cycle as the default and PAN-2079 is not present in this workspace; preserving the existing `feedback_delivery_needs_you` surface behind the delayed policy avoids inventing UI scope.

autoDecisions.summary: Define drain points in `spawnAgent()` and `resumeAgent()` rather than only in dashboard restart replay.
autoDecisions.rationale: Those paths cover CLI starts, dashboard starts, manual resumes, and Deacon auto-resume, which is the required deterministic pull guarantee.

items.title: Define issue-role mailbox metadata over `.pan/feedback/` files

expected_outputs: agent-mailbox tests pass and prove metadata parsing, legacy feedback fallback, and state transitions

narrative.Action: Create a focused mailbox helper module that reads and writes mailbox metadata embedded in `.pan/feedback/*.md` files. The metadata must include `issueId`, `role`, `source`, `summary`, `actionRequired`, `state`, `createdAt`, optional `deliveredAt`, optional `acknowledgedAt`, and the feedback file path. Provide helpers to list mailbox items for `{ issueId, role }`, mark `pending -> delivered`, mark `delivered -> acknowledged`, treat legacy numbered feedback files with no metadata as `pending` while their review/test status still requires action, and preserve markdown readability. Update `writeFeedbackFile()` only enough to create metadata for new feedback files; do not add a separate mailbox archive or durable queue.

items.title: Given a new feedback file, `writeFeedbackFile()` creates a `.pan/feedback/NNN-*.md` file containing parseable mailbox metadata addressed to `issueId` and role `work` with state `pending`.
Given an existing numbered feedback markdown file without metadata, the mailbox reader returns it as a `pending` item when the corresponding review/test status still requires action.
When mark-delivered or mark-acknowledged runs twice for the same item, the file remains valid markdown and the state transition is idempotent.
Given the mailbox module public API, TypeScript callers can create, list, mark-delivered, and mark-acknowledged mailbox items using `issueId` and `role` parameters without providing an `agentId`.
Route feedback producers through issue-role mailbox delivery

expected_outputs: feedback producer tests pass and assert durable queue entries contain issueId and role, not agentId

narrative.Action: Replace agent-id durable feedback delivery with issue+role delivery. In `pending-feedback.ts`, change `PendingFeedbackDelivery` so durable records store `issueId`, `role: 'work'`, `kind`, `filePath`, `message`, `createdAt`, and delivery policy timestamps, but not `agentId`. In `routes/workspaces.ts deliverQueuedFeedback()`, enqueue by issue+role, attempt live delivery by resolving a current work agent at send time, and mark the mailbox item delivered only after the live notification succeeds. Update review/test/verification feedback producers that call `resolveIssueFeedbackTarget()` so a missing live agent leaves a pending mailbox item instead of immediately surfacing `needs_you`; live target lookup remains a push optimization.

items.title: Given review-blocked feedback, `deliverQueuedFeedback()` persists an issue+role queue record and does not persist `agentId` in the durable pending-feedback store.
When a live work agent exists, the producer sends the existing short feedback pointer through `messageAgent()` and marks the mailbox item `delivered` after the send succeeds.
When no live work agent exists, feedback producers leave the mailbox item `pending` and return without calling `surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou()` immediately.
When review/test status no longer requires action, restart replay deletes the obsolete feedback queue entry and does not call `messageAgent()`.
Drain mailbox items during work-agent spawn and resume

expected_outputs: spawn/resume drain tests pass for fresh spawn, manual resume, and Deacon auto-resume

narrative.Action: Add a mailbox-drain step to the prompt construction path for work/strike agents. For `spawnAgent()`, after the base prompt and spawn-time memory are assembled but before the prompt file is written, append a concise mailbox section listing every pending or delivered-but-action-required `{ issueId, role:'work' }` item with absolute file path, source, summary, and explicit instruction to read the file before continuing. For `resumeAgent()`, wrap the default or caller-supplied resume message with the same mailbox section before delivery. Mark drained items delivered/acknowledged idempotently according to the mailbox helper contract. Deacon auto-resume must not need special delivery code; its existing `resumeAgent(agentId)` call must receive the drain.

items.title: Given a pending mailbox item before `spawnAgent()`, the generated initial prompt contains the feedback file's absolute path, source, summary, and a read-before-continue instruction.
Given a pending mailbox item before `resumeAgent()`, the delivered resume prompt contains the same mailbox section before normal continuation text.
When Deacon auto-resumes a stopped work agent with pending review/test feedback, the resume path drains the mailbox without calling a separate push-only feedback path.
When an already-delivered action-required item is drained again, the prompt includes it once and the mailbox state update remains idempotent.
Escalate undelivered action-required mail only after the policy window

expected_outputs: fake-timer escalation tests pass and prove no immediate needs_you marker is written

narrative.Action: Add a Deacon patrol helper that scans action-required mailbox items still `pending` past the policy window. Default the window to one patrol cycle using Cloister config, with tests using fake timers. The helper should first try to find or resume an eligible work agent through existing resume gates; if none exists or none spawns by the deadline, call the operator fallback. Because PAN-2079's operator inbox surface is not present in this workspace, route through the existing `surfaceIssueFeedbackNeedsYou()`/`markWorkspaceStuck()` mechanism but only from this delayed branch and include structured details for future PAN-2079 adapter replacement.

items.title: Given pending action-required mail created at time T and no live agent, the first delivery attempt returns without setting `stuckReason: feedback_delivery_needs_you`.
When an eligible agent spawns or resumes before the one-patrol deadline, the Deacon helper observes the delivered/acknowledged mailbox item and does not escalate.
When no eligible agent exists after the one-patrol deadline, the helper sets `feedback_delivery_needs_you` exactly once with issue id, role, source, summary, and feedback path details.
The policy-window test suite produces the escalation outcome by calling `vi.useFakeTimers()` and advancing timers, with no real wall-clock wait in the default test run.
Comment pending mailbox items during close-out before teardown

expected_outputs: close-out tests pass and prove pending mail is commented before workspace teardown

narrative.Action: Before close-out removes the workspace, read pending mailbox items for the issue and post one tracker comment if any remain. The comment must use the issue's prescribed stale-warning framing: `During close-out the system identified N undelivered message(s): ... These were never delivered to a working agent. If this issue is reopened: treat them as likely stale — but consider whether an uncaught message contributed to a premature closure. Do not treat them as current instructions.` Include source, summary, timestamp, and path for each item. Keep workspace teardown responsible for removing `.pan/feedback/`; do not copy files into an archive.

items.title: Given two pending mailbox items at close-out, the tracker comment lists both items with source, summary, timestamp, and the stale-warning text.
When close-out runs, the pending-mail comment step executes before the workspace removal step that deletes `.pan/feedback/`.
When there are no pending mailbox items, close-out posts no mailbox comment and preserves the existing close-out comment behavior.
Close-out creates no mailbox archive files outside the normal tracker comment.
Given tracker history contains the close-out stale-warning comment, the next planning/work kickoff prompt omits that comment from current mailbox instructions.
